question.problem:
Consider the curve defined parametrically as 

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y={sin}^{2}⁡t,\,t\in [0,\pi ].
$$

What integral gives the surface area generated when this curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis?
question.worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi y\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since our curve is given in parametric form, we have

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

We are told that the limits of integration are from ${t}_{1}=0$ to ${t}_{2}=\pi .$ 

Computing the derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({sin}^{2}⁡t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡t\sqrt{{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡t\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡t+4{sin}^{2}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡t\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡t(1+{cos}^{2}⁡t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡t\cdot |2\operatorname{sin}⁡t|\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }{sin}^{3}⁡t\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
